images.caption:
The Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River is a 35-mile-long (56 km) tributary of the Cosumnes River in the Sierra Nevada of California. The river originates in the Stanislaus National Forest near the town of Pinecrest and flows generally west through the Eldorado National Forest to its confluence with the North Fork of the Cosumnes River near the town of Acampo. The Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River is a popular destination for fishing, camping, and hiking.
The geology of the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River is characterized by the presence of sedimentary rocks, including sandstone, shale, and limestone. The river is also home to a variety of wildlife, including fish, birds, and mammals.
The history of the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River is closely tied to the history of the Native Americans who lived in the area. The river was a major source of water and food for the Native Americans, and they used it for fishing, swimming, and transportation. The first European to see the river was John C. Fremont in 1844.
In the 19th century, the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River was used for mining and agriculture. The river was also a popular destination for tourists who came to enjoy the scenery and the outdoor activities. 
Photo by Jesse Pluim, BLM

images.caption: Carnegie Library, 557 Lincoln St. Roseville, CA. Photo captured Nikon CoolPix S570 at 12k resolution. This image was captured for the purpose of matching a black & white photo take from the same camera position circa 1912, to be used as a "Then and Now" photo comparison of the same subject. This photo was favored over others due to the U.S. and California flags caught blowing in the light breeze. No alterations have been applied to the original image other than cropping. This image is being used in the website for the Roseville Historical Society, located in Roseville, CA.
